scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9106: A user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports they have completely
lost connectivity to the partner network -- they cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2) in
the peer AS since this morning. The team insists the inter-AS physical link
between router1 and router2 is down and want it re-cabled. Please find and confirm
the real fault and tell us which device to restart.

injection.action: kill the BGP routing daemon (and its watchdog) on router1

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on router1: its BGP routing daemon (bgpd) has been killed, so
the eBGP session between router1 and router2 drops and router1 loses/withdraws
the inter-AS routes. With no route to the peer AS, pc1 (195.11.14.2) cannot reach
pc2 (200.1.1.2). The ticket MISDESCRIBES the cause as a physical link failure,
but the inter-AS link is UP: router1's eth0 (the inter-AS interface to router2)
is up and carrier is fine -- this is a dead daemon, not a cut cable.

The correct diagnosis identifies router1 (bgpd down) as the faulty device and
explicitly distinguishes a daemon crash from a link failure: the inter-AS
interface (router1 eth0) is UP, so the user's "the physical link is down"
hypothesis is wrong. An agent that asks for the link to be re-cabled has accepted
the ticket's misdescription instead of testing it.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): bgpd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router bgp` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists bgpd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the bgp configuration is missing/empty on router1" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR/bgpd on router1 (`service frr restart`). Once bgpd is running again,
the eBGP session to router2 re-establishes, router1 re-learns and re-advertises
the inter-AS prefixes, and pc1 reaches pc2 normally. No re-cabling is needed --
the link was up the whole time.
scoring_axes: must-identify-bgpd-down: identifies bgpd on router1 is down, not a physical link failure
bonus-rules-out-link: notes router1's inter-AS interface (eth0) is UP, distinguishing a daemon crash from the ticket's "link down" cause

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The `bgpd` daemon (FRR's BGP process) on router1, along with its supervisor `watchfrr`, has crashed and is in a FAILED state.

**Mechanism:** With `bgpd` dead on router1, the BGP session between router1 (AS unknown/unconfigured at runtime) and router2 (AS 2) can never be established. Router2 correctly shows its single BGP neighbor permanently stuck in the `Active` state — it keeps trying to open a TCP session to router1's BGP port but receives no answer. Because no BGP session exists, neither router exchanges prefixes: router1 never learns the 200.1.1.0/24 prefix reachable via router2, and router2 never learns the 195.11.14.0/24 prefix reachable via router1.

**Localization:** router1 — `bgpd` process is FAILED, `watchfrr` (the FRR daemon supervisor that would auto-restart it) is also FAILED. `zebra`, `mgmtd`, and `staticd` remain running, which is why the physical link and L3 forwarding infrastructure are intact enough to generate ICMP "Destination Net Unreachable" responses — the routers simply have no route entries for the far-side subnets.

**Root cause:** The `bgpd` daemon on router1 has crashed and was not restarted (watchfrr also failed), eliminating the BGP session and all inter-AS route exchange.

**Fix:** Restart the FRR service on router1 (`service frr restart` or `systemctl restart frr`). This will bring up both `watchfrr` and `bgpd`, re-establish the BGP session with router2, and restore full route exchange. No re-cabling is needed — the physical link is healthy.

per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly states bgpd (and watchfrr) on router1 has crashed and rules out a physical link failure, noting the interface/L3 forwarding remain up and no re-cabling is needed.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-link: notes router1's inter-AS interface (eth0) is UP, distinguishing a daemon crash from the ticket's "link down" cause
per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly distinguishes a dead bgpd from a physical link failure and states the physical link is healthy (no re-cabling needed and L3/ICMP responses intact), which satisfies the axis requirement that the inter-AS link is UP.
The agent's remediation matches the expected fix—restart FRR/bgpd on router1 (e.g., service frr restart) to restore the BGP session and routes.

The investigation log directly shows bgpd and watchfrr FAILED on router1, router2 in BGP Active, and ICMP 'Destination Net Unreachable' responses from the routers — the writeup's claims follow from these observations and correctly attributes loss of routes to the dead bgpd. The diagnosis, causal chain, and recommended fix are all justified by the presented evidence.
